# Missing-middle rule research: lessons register (Oct–Nov 2026)

What five states of local-rule coding (MN, NC, OH, TX, OR) taught us, and what the MM agent swarm does about each
lesson. Sources were read in full on 2026-11-17: the rules-related `logbook.d/` fragments, `LOGBOOK.md`, the
HANDOFF decisions log, `docs/build/manual-ordinance-*.md`, the state data plans and readiness notes,
`docs/research/ordinances/` (README, research issues, second-coder sheets and decisions, corrections, evidence
register, lookup sheets), the MM causal diagram and uptake evidence, the `tx_*`, `nc_second_coder*`, `mn_*`
scripts, `src/lotline/model/rule_tags.py`, and the four 2026-11-11 MM rule-check reports (in git history only:
`c3589b04` NC, `e854583a` TX, `6c0d6f5f` OR, `bdef3d03` MN/OH). `lbd/` = `logbook.d/`.

Each lesson has an ID used in the design (`DESIGN.md`) and in the agent prompts, and a **Swarm response**.

## R: retrieval

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-1 | **Official code hosts block scripts.** Batch 1 read 0/28 Municode, 0/14 American Legal, 0/7 Granicus, 0/5 Laserfiche, 0/5 CivicWeb links. Municode serves a Cloudflare challenge (its robots.txt itself 403s); eCode360's robots.txt disallows ClaudeBot; American Legal 403s even where robots allows; enCodePlus disallows `/regs/` for AI agents. | `batch1-2026-10-20.json`; `lbd/2026-10-23-ws-tx-s4-rules.md`; `scripts/archive/tx_rules_21_40.py`; `manual-ordinance-lookups.md` | Retrieval agent checks robots for our token *and* Claude's (`fetch.AGENT_TOKENS`), classifies code-host walls (`access.CODE_HOSTS`) and hands them off with a host-specific browser tip. Discovery goes to the routes below first. |
| R-2 | **City sites 403 at scale.** 25 of 40 NC city homepages answer scripts with 403; Durham ordinance PDFs, Fort Worth, Houston Permitting, Bend, Minneapolis LIMS (403 even for robots.txt). | `lbd/2026-10-21-ws-nc-4-rules-research.md`; `manual-ordinance-pdfs-batch1.md` | A 403 on robots.txt closes the host for the run (`fetch.get`). |
| R-3 | **What worked:** the Legistar Web API (`webapi.legistar.com/v1/<client>/matters/...`, 5 of 12 links read), plain CDN PDFs (14 of 16 govstack), Wayback copies of official files, county/BOCC agendas for effective dates, Laserfiche `ElectronicFile.aspx?docid=` direct links. | `batch1`; `lbd/2026-10-26-ws-oh-7-rules.md`; NC report `c3589b04` | Source-discovery agent ranks routes in this order and records each try in `searched`. |
| R-4 | **Wayback is the predecessor-code library.** Wake Forest's 1977 ordinance (amended to 2010), Morrisville ZO 2010, Burlington 1971 §32.9, League City's 2011 use table all came from the archive. It can be offline or rate-limit (HTTP 429 at Dayton). | NC/TX reports; `lbd/2026-10-26-ws-oh-7-rules.md` | Prior-cap evidence (M-2) may cite `source_kind: archive`; an archive outage is a `not_found` blocker, not a guess. |
| R-5 | **Never retry a refused fetch another way.** Medford OR (re-fetched with plain curl) and Scott County MN (browser user agent → Cloudflare 403) were recorded incidents; the copies were deleted. A Charlotte subagent fetched three robots-disallowed PDFs; San Antonio's `/api/` was called before reading robots. | README "Process incidents"; `lbd/2026-10-20-ws-nc-4-adu-rules.md`; `lbd/2026-10-23-ws-tx-data-plan.md` | Hard rule in every agent prompt; `fetch.get` makes one attempt with the project user agent and never changes headers. Only `python -m lotline.rule_agents.mm fetch` or WebFetch after the robots check may touch the network. |
| R-6 | **The browser agent was the only route that read Municode/amlegal at scale without bypassing anything**: one page at a time, stop on any challenge → 74 confirmed, 9 manual, 5 partly, 2 contradicted. | README §WS-ADU-RULES | Optional browser stage, run by the orchestrator in the main session (unattended allowed, Ben 2026-11-17), never by background subagents; stops at any challenge or CAPTCHA. |
| R-7 | **Mirrors are undated.** Zoneomics (robots allow all) was TX's workhorse for places 21–40, but its text is the current code: Lubbock's 2024 mirror text differed from the 2023 as-adopted text. 37 TX MM rows still carry "read on the zoneomics mirror only". | `tx_rules_21_40.py`; `tx-second-coder-lubbock-2026-11-07.md` | `source_kind: mirror`; mirror-only values cannot be `high` confidence and get the FLAG note (`findings.check`, `rows`). |
| R-8 | **Wrong-place sources.** Canton GA for Canton OH, Thomasville GA, Newbern TN, Columbia MO for Columbia Heights MN, Brooklyn Park for Brooklyn Center; wrong GEOIDs from a reviewer. | `lbd/2026-11-01-ws-nc-second-coder.md`; `manual-ordinance-pdfs-batch1.md` | Verifier confirms the place name *and* state appear in each source; enumerator fixes the GEOID from the place list, coders never type it. |
| R-9 | **Budgets run out.** NC's shared 200-call search budget ran out early; batch 1 cost ~3.5M tokens for 23 cities (~107k per city in the pilot). | `lbd/2026-10-20-ws-nc-4-adu-rules.md`; batch-1 fragment | Per-place budgets and stop rules in every agent (DESIGN §4); a place that hits its budget becomes a hand-off, not a longer search. |
| R-10 | **Records by request are a dead end.** Ben files no records requests and emails no staff. | memory `no-records-requests`; every MM rule-check report | `records_request_only` closes as `no_usable_source` at once; no task is written (`handoff.task_for`). |

## P: PDFs and documents

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| P-1 | **Use-table columns misread from the PDF text layer were the top MM error** (League City RSF-5 withdrawn; McAllen columns lost; Rochester R-1 cells "confirm visually on p. 96"; Burlington "columns read by text position"). | `config/reforms/tx.csv` TX-4841980; `mn_mm_batch1_2026_11_02.py` | Any value that rests on a table cell must say so in evidence `section` ("Table 2-1, row Two-family, column R-4") and, for PDFs, be read as the page image (Read tool `pages`) by the coder; the verifier re-reads that page as an image. |
| P-2 | **Scans need OCR** (Cincinnati Ord. 199-2024, Euclid, two CCITT fax PDFs). We ship no OCR engine. | LB-071; MN report `bdef3d03` | Claude reads scan pages as images; if the scan is unreadable or over ~20 pages of scan → `scanned_pdf` hand-off. |
| P-3 | **Unsigned drafts look final** ("Ordinance No. XXX-XX", blank adoption blocks, "[insert effective date]"): St. Louis Park, Eagan Ord. 528, Burnsville 2020, Duluth. | `mn-second-coder-decisions-2026-11-02.csv` | `findings.draft_markers(text)`; a draft can support `announced_date` only, never adoption or effective dates. |
| P-4 | **Code books show current text, not when a cell changed** ("the PDF has no amendment history"). | `tx-second-coder-2026-10-30.csv` | Dates come from the ordinance, minutes or the code's history note, never from the code edition date (DT-2). |
| P-5 | **Large files and download-only links** (over 10 MB; letstalk download notices; MN 403 on download but readable in a browser). | `mn-downloaded-pdf-inventory-2026-11-02.csv` | `js_only`/`http_403_waf` hand-off with "opens in a browser" tip. |

## D: dates

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| DT-1 | **Effective beats adoption**, from each state's rule (Ohio R.C. 731.29 or charter: 30 days, emergency on passage; Minn. Stat. §645.15; Oregon 30-day clauses). Computed dates must say "(computed)": Columbus 2025-12-25 computed, 2025-12-24 per the city. | LB-096; `oh-lookups-brief-2026-11-01.md`; `lbd/2026-10-26-ws-oh-7-rules.md` | Coder records both dates with separate evidence; a computed effective date gets "(computed: rule …)" in notes and `date_basis` stays `dated` only if adoption is quoted. State default rules go in the run brief (`state_rules` in DESIGN §3). |
| DT-2 | **Code and rewrite dates are not events.** Most lookups give the date a code was adopted, not when duplexes first became legal. Second coding flipped Wake Forest, Morrisville, Sanford, Burlington, League City to `[predates]`; Sanford's date was a land-use-plan date; Denton's belonged to an unrelated amendment. Without those NC events θ fell 0.12 → 0.013. | NC/TX reports; `lbd/2026-11-11-ws-mm-review.md` | The prior-cap check (M-2) is mandatory for every dated event; equal caps → `predates`. |
| DT-3 | **Treatment date choices**: Austin HOME vote 2023-12-07, in effect 12-18, applications from 2024-02-05 → coded 2024-02-05. | LB-068 | When applications open later than the effective date, coder records both and codes the application date as `effective_date`, quoting it. |
| DT-4 | **Rules are read on 1 July**: a date doubt matters only if it crosses 1 July (Portland RIP 2021-08-01 counts from 2022; OR medium tier 2021-06-30). | `rule_tags.py`; OR report | Reconciler grades a date diff that does not cross a 1 July boundary as minor in its adjudication note. |
| DT-5 | **Tags are the engine's contract** (`rule_tags.py`): `[predates]` never an event (in force from 1990); `[earliest-known]` or blank adoption → event, dropped in a sensitivity; on/before 2010-01-01 read as before the window; `DATE UNCONFIRMED` → event, dropped in a sensitivity; `[standards]` → dose class S. Action text like "tag [predates]" in notes was once read as a real tag (Cottage Grove). | `rule_tags.py`; `lbd/2026-11-02-ws-mn-13-readiness.md` | Coders set `date_basis`; only `rows.py` writes tags, first in the notes; notes text from agents may not contain bracketed tags (`findings.check` rejects them). |
| DT-6 | **Dateless rows are dangerous** (East Bethel would enter as a 2010 adopter). | `lbd/2026-10-20-ws-mn-5-adu-histories.md` | `effective_date` is required; no date → hand-off, not a row. |
| DT-7 | **State preemption** is coded by a statute-driven generator (`or_state_reform_rows.py`), not by local research; OR deadlines 2021-06-30 / 2022-06-30 / 2025-06-30 / 2027-01-01; tiers near a population threshold follow PSU certified estimates. Blank adoption dates on 111 SB 458 rows nearly dropped all Oregon (fixed by D-092 §1). | `lbd/2026-11-04-ws-or-state-law.md`; D-092 | Out of scope for the local swarm: the run brief lists state-law rows already coded; coders code local rules only and note "state law also applies". Local early/late adopters get their own rows. |
| DT-8 | **Pending rules** (Findlay 2027-01-01, Cleveland Heights) are `status = pending`; moratoria coded `suspended` were silently dropped by engine filters (Blaine). | `lbd/2026-10-26-ws-oh-7-rules.md`; `lbd/2026-11-16-adu-uncoded-rules.md` | `findings.check` forces `pending` for future dates; moratoria are flagged for Ben, not coded by the MM swarm. |

## S: second coding

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| S-1 | **The sheets were not blind.** TX/NC/MN reviewers saw `coded_as` and checked it; only the OR state-law coder coded without seeing rows. | `docs/research/ordinances/*second-coder*.csv` | Coder B gets only the place, the state brief and the source list, never coder A's file (DESIGN §5). |
| S-2 | **"Could not read the source" is not agreement.** TX: 74 of 78 "partly" verdicts were boilerplate; those rows stayed `single_coder`. | `tx_second_coder_2026_10_30.py` | A rule coder B could not open counts as an unpaired major diff, and the row is `single_coder` unless the verifier re-found every quote. |
| S-3 | **What second coding caught**: NC 8 yes / 44 partly / 14 no (8 → `[predates]`, 5 new rows); MN 14/92/8 (28 → DATE UNCONFIRMED, 2 false events deleted: Hopkins 2024 accessory footprint, Grant 2016 health-care-dwelling opt-out); TX corrections 35 (32 accepted); the 2026-11-11 MM checks flipped 5 events and cut Houston's cap 8 → 4. | decisions CSVs; MM reports | Reconciler classifies diffs into the same categories (recodification, date, cap, coverage, false event, new rule) for the run report. |
| S-4 | **Same-model second coders are not fully independent.** | `or_state_reform_rows.py` SECOND_NOTE | Coder B runs on a different model tier than coder A where possible and must search independently; `coder_2` records the model. Ben's or Codex review remains the gold standard for high-leverage places. |
| S-5 | **Proposals, not edits; append-only, idempotent apply scripts**; renames when the year moves; a recommendation nearly overwrote Ben's Hugo lookup. | `tx-corrections-*.csv`; `lbd/2026-10-30-ws-tx-wrapup.md` | The swarm writes a candidate table and a diff against `config/reforms`; it never edits config. Ben merges. |
| S-6 | **Check top-leverage places first.** The MM fit rested on Houston, then six NC towns, then Oregon; one wrong row flips the result. | `lbd/2026-10-20-ws-engine-mm-estimate.md`; `lbd/2026-11-12-ws-mm-run4-5.md` | Enumerator sorts places by population (a leverage proxy); the run brief may pass a priority list. |

## M: missing-middle traps

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| M-1 | **`unit_cap` = most principal homes allowed on one single-family-zoned lot by the rule.** Bonus caps go in notes (Portland 4, "6 with 50% affordable"); the cap that holds across the covered districts is coded (St. Louis Park 3). The dose grades 2 → 1/3, 3 → 2/3, ≥ 4 → 1. | `estimate_mm.py`; `config/reforms/or.csv` | Coder prompt spells this out; `unit_cap` ≥ 1 enforced. |
| M-2 | **An event is a cap rise over the prior cap** (D-042, D-092 §1). Houston duplexes and Austin SF-3 two-family were already legal; Austin's old "two-family" was really an ADU; Lubbock's old R-2 already allowed duplexes. | `lbd/2026-11-03-ws-engine-14-mm-anchor.md`; `lbd/2026-11-07-ws-mm-followups.md` | `RuleFinding.prior_cap` with evidence is required for every dated event; `prior_cap ≥ unit_cap` fails the check. |
| M-3 | **"None" rows** (`unit_cap = 1`) code a place as untreated on evidence: a control, never an event (TX 31, MN 3). A draft once counted Rochester's one-home row as an event. Districts that already allow duplexes narrow the none row's coverage (Rochester, Brooklyn Park → R-1 only). | `rule_tags.none_places`; `mn-second-coder-decisions-2026-11-02.csv` | Coders must code a none row (with evidence from the current use table) when nothing allows 2–4 homes; a place with neither a rule nor a blocker fails the check. |
| M-4 | **Two-family districts are not MM** (Amarillo R-3; Abilene: district text governs over the use matrix). **Revised by Ben 2026-11-17:** a 2→3 (or higher) rise in a two-family district also counts, matching the coded Minneapolis row (R1;R1A;R2;R2B); existing coded rows are not changed. | `lbd/2026-10-30-ws-tx-ben-lookups.md`; Ben, 2026-11-17 (PR #469) | Coder prompt: `coverage_zones` lists every residential district whose cap rose to `unit_cap` under the rule, single-family and two-family alike; `prior_cap` is the lowest cap any covered district had just before (usually the single-family 1). A two-family district whose cap did not rise is left out. |
| M-5 | **by_right**: P, PS, SR, staff approval, "limited use (Director)" count as by right; CUP/SUP/rezoning is `False`. Corner-lot-only or one-per-block-face limits go in `coverage`, not `by_right`. | Lubbock md; NC report | Coder prompt table of approval codes. |
| M-6 | **Coverage decides whether a rule counts**: a rule must cover at least half the eligible parcels (`calibrate_mm.prior_cap`); corridor-only rules (Cincinnati) are not fit events; zone lists must use district names current at the row's date (Lubbock R-1→SF-2, Wake Forest R-10→GR5). | `estimate_mm._mm_coverage`; NC MM report | `coverage_zones` as written at the time; renames go in notes with the crosswalk. |
| M-7 | **Standards reforms stay in**: Houston's 2023 MUR → `[standards]`, cap = the local-street cap (4, not 8). | D-092 §1b; memory `mm-keep-always-allowed` | `standards_only = True` (cap unchanged or blank) writes `[standards]`. |
| M-8 | **Always-allowed places stay in the fit** (`[predates]` with cap ≥ 2: League City, Houston, Dayton 2006, Grove City 1979, Apex 2000, New Bern 1996). Ben: "Keep League City and Houston" applies to every such place. | D-092 §1b; memory `mm-keep-always-allowed` | Coders code the pre-window rule explicitly as `predates` (never drop the place); the run report counts always-allowed places. |
| M-9 | **Concurrent reforms are separate components** (Minneapolis parking 2021 beside the 2020 three-unit rule; SCAD). | `config/reforms/mn.csv`; causal diagram §2 | Coders list concurrent parking/lot-size/process changes in `notes` as leads; they are not coded by the MM swarm. |
| M-10 | **Holdout leakage**: research pages showed post-reform counts (Bend, Clackamas, Florence, a St. Paul staff report). | `lbd/2026-11-04-ws-or-local-rules.md`; README incidents | Agents never record permit or housing counts in findings; the run brief lists holdout places, whose rules may be coded but whose outcome numbers must not be written down. |

## H: human hand-offs

| ID | Lesson | Evidence | Swarm response |
|---|---|---|---|
| H-1 | **Wide per-place fill-in tables stayed empty** (MN 1/33, NC 0/36, OH 0/47, ADU 0/114). | `*-lookups-todo.csv` | One task per blocked source, with only the 2–4 fields it would settle, priority-sorted (`handoff.tasks`). |
| H-2 | **What got filled**: long-format logs (`manual-lookups.csv`, 71 rows), sheets keyed by `reform_id`, and Ben's own agentic workbooks with official PDFs. Fastest: Ben pasting official links in chat; one-at-a-time confirmations with ordinance number + adoption + effective. | `manual-lookups.csv`; `lbd/2026-11-02-ws-mn-13-readiness.md` | Tasks are written so a person *or Ben's browser agent* can work them: start URL, host tip, closed answers, acceptance rule; `ingest` reads them back. |
| H-3 | **AI search summaries without a primary source became tag debt** (67 of 71 manual-lookup rows). | `manual-lookups.csv` notes | A `found` answer needs a verbatim quote and the URL it came from (`handoff.answer_problems`); `search_summary` is lead-only (`findings.LEAD_ONLY`). |
| H-4 | **Yes/no columns can't say "by right only in R-2" or "corner lots only".** | B-notes §6 | Answer columns are `max_homes_per_single_family_lot`, `by_right`, `districts`, plus free `notes`. |
| H-5 | **Ambiguous stays unknown; unresolved stays unresolved** (Ben 2026-10-20). | `docs-ben-manual-lookups` | `result` has three closed answers; `not_found`/`no_usable_source` leave the field blank (D-022 draws). |
